speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; could you tell me how long this swelling has been present and if it follows a specific activity?

Also, do you experience pain, redness, or warmth in the knee, and does it feel stiff in the morning?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Uric_Acid

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial inflammatory markers and blood work are normal, which is helpful. Given your family history and the isolated joint swelling, could you describe the specific type of crystals seen on your previous ultrasound or X-ray, or have you experienced any sudden, severe attacks of pain in this joint before? Also, is there any visible redness or warmth currently?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular). The patient is an 18-month-old boy with unilateral knee swelling, a family history of autoimmune conditions, and normal inflammatory markers, which fits the typical presentation of oligoarticular JIA. I am requesting an X-ray of the right knee to rule out other causes and an MRI to assess for bone marrow edema or synovitis. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Knee_XRay, Right_Knee_MRI.
